methods.description: Identify interviewer/identification pressure and propose confidential, neutral administration suited to respondents.
Identify missing responses or incomplete observational records; explain possible differences and restore coverage without guaranteeing removal of bias.

# Bias in Sampling Methods

+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|- **Sampling Bias**|
+=========================+=========================+=============================+
|- A biased, or unrepresentative, sample doesn't accurately represent the|
|population.|
||
|- Sources of sampling bias:|
+-------------------------+-------------------------+-----------------------------+
|**Sampling Bias**|**Description**|**Example**|
+-------------------------+-------------------------+-----------------------------+
|Selection bias|The selected group|Measuring average height of|
||misrepresents the|15-year-olds by only|
||population.|surveying the basketball|
|||team.|
+-------------------------+-------------------------+-----------------------------+
|Small Sample Size|A small sample may miss|Surveying only three people|
||population variety.|about a new highway.|
+-------------------------+-------------------------+-----------------------------+
|Volunteer Bias|The sampling method|A study on dietary habits|
||relies on people|attracting only|
||volunteering to|health-conscious|
||participate.|volunteers.|
+-------------------------+-------------------------+-----------------------------+
|Survivorship Bias|Considers only|Evaluating the success of|
||successful cases,|businesses only by looking|
||ignoring failures.|at those still in|
|||operation, ignoring those|
|||that have failed.|
+-------------------------+-------------------------+-----------------------------+

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
|- **Identify** sampling bias|
+===================================+===================================+
|a.  A survey was conducted to|b.  Mr Ding wants to know the|
|determine the average income|percentage of school students|
|of residents in a particular|who have maths as their|
|city. The survey only|favourite subject.\|
|included responses from|He surveys the Year 12 Maths|
|residents who lived in|Extension class.|
|wealthy harbourside||
|neighbourhoods.||
+-----------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
|c.  The government wanted to know|d.  Investigating the religious|
|farmers' opinions on a new|beliefs of Australians by|
|road.\|surveying people at shopping|
|They asked 2 farmers out of a|centres on Sunday mornings.|
|community of 500.||
+-----------------------------------+-----------------------------------+

sourceReview.excerpt:
# Questionnaire Design

+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|- **Questioning Bias**|
+===================================+====================================================+
|Bias can also come from poorly worded questions in a survey.|
+-----------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------+
|**Questioning Bias**|**Example**|
+-----------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------+
|Leading question|Implying a preferred answer:|
|||
||"most people think that..."\|
||Using emotional language:\|
||"do you agree that this policy is brilliant?"\|
||Giving one-sided contextual information:|
|||
||"given the new metro will cost \$10 billion,|
||should we build it?"|
+-----------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------+
|Ambiguous questions|A question that asks how often someone goes to the|
||gym but does not specify the time frame.|
|||
||Questions that are too open ended lead to bias|
||because participants can interpret it in different|
||ways.|
+-----------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------+
|Not providing enough choices|A question that asks how many hours of homework|
||per week, with multiple choice response that|
||ranges from 1 to 4 hours.|
+-----------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------+

+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|- **Identify** Bias in questions|
+===================================+==============================================================================+
|a.  A questionnaire asks: Polls|b.  A questionnaire asks: Considering that many students dislike|
|show that 90% of customers|mathematics, should mathematics be made compulsory?|
|prefer the new Strawberry||
|Dream yogurt.\||
|What do you think?||
+-----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|c.  A questionnaire asks:|d.  A survey was conducted to estimate how much homework students do.\|
|Considering that almost all|From "a little" to "a lot."|
|high paying future jobs will||
|require some use of||
|mathematics, should||
|mathematics be made||
|compulsory?||
+-----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|e.  A survey asks "what do you|f.  ![](media/Data Analysis/media/image191.png){width="2.8295636482939632in"|
|think about the government's|height="0.7001520122484689in"}|
|evil plan to build new||
|apartments in Croydon?"||
+-----------------------------------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
